items.note: the paper's opening exhibit and its only free-hand line drawing: a side elevation of one hop with the transmitter at the left and the receiver at the right, a dotted band standing in for the ionosphere, the curved ray labelled S inside a bisector construction, and the symbolic labels D1, D2, h0, hr, theta, theta-prime and P_proj. section_path: Results from Geographic Locations in Part III

note: Thirty-one regions across 17 of 31 pages, and every region is an exhibit or a pasted equation: 18 captioned figures, 8 captioned tables, and five LaTeX display-equation blocks that the region detector measures as artwork (equations 3 to 10 on p10, 11 to 15 on p11, 18 on p13). The paper is a LaTeX report with MATLAB screenshots dropped in, so caption side is decided by exhibit kind and holds without exception - every figure caption below its artwork, every table caption above its grid - and both kinds share one numbering grammar, 'Figure N.' and 'Table N.', with no roman, no colon and no glued number. The tables are the tidiest part of the paper: eight grids, one template, an outer box with a vertical at every cell boundary, no zebra shading anywhere, no merged cell, no diagonal header, no note line, no continuation across a page, and centred rather than decimal-aligned figures. Only width varies, half for the three-column power grids and the four-column sensitivity grids, full for the five-column distance grids, and units move between header, stub and caption in a pattern that is consistent except on the one grid with empty cells. The figures split into three drawing tools. Five box plots share one glyph. Three terrain surfaces are the only three-dimensional exhibits and the only ones with a labelled z axis. Four exhibits carry colour bars - the two electron-density disks of Figure 8 and the three cell grids of Figures 12 to 14 - and nothing else does, so colour encodes a field only where the axes are a parameter plane. The three cell grids are worth flagging: 12 and 13 share axes to the tick, but 14 steps elevation by 10 degrees and frequency by 5 MHz, so the three plates in one column cannot be read across. Two figures are captured web basemaps with a map pin and a single arrow, printed without axes or scale, and those are the two the text never cites. The appendix is a plate section announced entirely from the body, 10 to 15 pages ahead, with no cross-reference inside it; the paper's own citations are the weakest part of the record, since the prose prints 'the numerical values are shown in 1' twice, leaving two tables announced without a number and two more never announced. One caption states a result (Figure 15) and one caption covers only half of its own exhibit (Figure 11, whose left panel plots water conditions the caption does not mention).
rules: Caption side is decided by exhibit kind and never varies within the kind: all eighteen figure captions print BELOW their artwork and all eight table captions print ABOVE their grid, although both kinds share one numbering grammar [caption.position].

Numbering is 'Figure N.' and 'Table N.' with a period and a space on every one of the twenty-six exhibits, so the paper has exactly one label form and a reader can grep either kind with the same pattern [caption.numbering].

The paper has one table template applied eight times: an outer box, a vertical rule at every cell boundary, a horizontal under the header and between the body rows. Not one grid is booktabs, and the absence is uniform across both problem parts and the sensitivity section [table.rule_style].

No grid shades alternating rows, merges a cell, or prints a diagonal header - zero instances across all eight tables - so this paper is the cleanest counter-example in the lane to the idea that merged headers come with multi-condition grids [table.zebra].

Numeric cells are centred, never decimal-aligned: the 2-decimal power grids and the 5-decimal distance grids both centre, and Table 5's 1085.87 and 810.67 do not share a decimal column even though they sit one above the other [table.decimal_aligned].

Units ride in the header or the stub on seven of the eight grids and appear in the caption exactly once, on Table 5 ('Measured in km'), which is also the only grid with empty cells - so the unit convention breaks where the data are incomplete [table.units_in_header].

Width is the only table variable: half width for the two 3-column power grids, full width for everything else - 80 per cent of the column for the three 4-column sensitivity grids and about 100 for the four 5-column distance grids - and no grid continues onto a second page [table.width].

Colour bars appear only where the exhibit encodes a continuous field: the two electron-density disks of Figure 8 (each with its own bar) and the three cell grids 12 to 14. The five box plots and the three surfaces carry none, so colour encodes a quantity only on the four exhibits that plot a field over a parameter plane [geometry.colorbar].

Three-dimensional drawing is confined to the terrain model: Figures 2, 6 and 7 are all point-mesh surfaces with a normal arrow at each mesh point, all carry an inside legend at upper right, and all print Height (m), X distance (m) and Y distance (m) - the only exhibits in the paper whose z axis is labelled [geometry.three_d].

Box-and-whisker is the most-used family at five exhibits and all five use the same glyph - unfilled blue box, red median bar, black dashed whiskers with caps - so the paper runs one box template seven panels deep and spends its variety on the categorical axis instead [geometry.family].

Every appendix figure is announced from the body, 10 to 15 pages before it prints, and not one appendix page cites another exhibit: the plate section is written as if the body sentences were its only reading instructions [mention.lead_pages].

Five exhibits are never cited at all - the two captured basemaps (Figures 3 and 4) and three tables (2, 4 and 5) - so the uncited share is one ninth of the figures against three eighths of the tables, and the tables are the exhibits a reader is most likely to be sent to by a numberless sentence [mention.count].

Table citations are broken rather than absent: twice on p16 the prose prints 'the numerical values are shown in 1', so Tables 1 and 3 are announced without a number and Table 2 and Table 4 are never announced at all [mention.style].

One caption carries a second, concluding sentence (Figure 15's 'Calm distances are statistically different than both turbulent oceans'), and it is the only caption in the paper that states a result rather than naming a subject [caption.concludes].

The captions are subject labels and nothing else: no figure caption names a unit, a variable value, a condition or a parameter except Figure 13's 'a.k.a. Total Distance in km', which is also the only caption with two names for one quantity [caption.verbatim].

Figure 11 is the paper's one caption/panel mismatch: its caption names only terrain, while its left panel plots Calm Water against Turbulent Water - the comparison already made by Figure 10 - so half the exhibit answers a question its own title does not ask [caption.verbatim].

The two map exhibits are not model output at all but captured web basemaps with a pin and one arrow each, printed with no axes, no scale and no legend, so the distance a trajectory covers cannot be read off either exhibit [geometry.printed_numbers].
